messages.subject: bout.metric question
parts:
Hi Vincent,

We analyzed a small set of data using GGIR v. 1.2-8 and GGIR v. 1.5-12 to estimate MVPA.

One run used v. 1.2-8 with mvpa.2014=FALSE and closedbout=FALSE.
A second run used v. 1.5-12 with bout.metric=1 and closedbout=FALSE, and produced the same MVPA estimates as the first run.
A third run used v. 1.5-12 with bout.metric=2 and closedbout=FALSE, and produced higher MVPA estimates than the other two runs.

All runs used do.imp = FALSE.

Based on the documentation of bout.metric in the manual, we expected bout.metric=2 and closedbout=FALSE to match mvpa.2014=FALSE and closedbout=FALSE.

We want to be sure our understanding of the bout processing is correct. The manual version 1.5-12 states on page 24, on bout.metric = 1: "Here, the algorithm looks for 10 minute windows in which more than XX percent of the epochs are above mvpathreshold, and then counts the entire window as mvpa."

We're assuming that bout.metric = 1 with closedbout = FALSE does not count periods of inactivity within a 10-minute bout toward the total MVPA, even though this contradicts the manual. Is our interpretation correct?

Thanks.

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] bout.metric question
parts:
Hi Cathy,

About the differences between metric 1 and 2:

The best way to gain insight into the calculations is by studying the R code itself and/or experimenting with dummy data with function g.getbout() on its own.

The code for metric 2 only evaluates whether the bout criteria is met for an entire window and then counts all epochs within that window towards the bout, so including the inactivity breaks.

Metric 1 in combination with closedbout=FALSE, is different in that it only counts the epochs that meet the criteria towards MVPA. Hence why it is called closedbout=FALSE (the gaps in the bout are not closed). This is done by this fragment of the code "p[jmvpa:max(which(p < endi))]". Here, p are all the epochs for which the criteria is met. The alternative route (closedbout=TRUE) would lead to the following bit of code being used "p[jmvpa]:p[max(which(p < endi))]" here, the p is again used, but only to identify the beginning and end of the bout and everything in between is counted towards MVPA. 

This is why metric 2 provides longer bouts compared with metric 1 + closedbout=FALSE.

Note that closebout = TRUE only affects metrict 1, the other metrics are unaffected.

It might be that the manual does not exactly match this description. If you can advise on rewording that would be helpful.
Ideally, all these approaches should someday be described in a paper people can refer to..

Regarding your comment "A second run used v. 1.5-12 with bout.metric=1 and closedbout=FALSE, and produced the same MVPA estimates as the first run.": This is expected because it was a change of terminology as I explained in the manual.

Vincent

Hi Vincent,

Thank you for your reply. We did run comparisons using different combinations of the settings, as you suggested. And your explanation confirms our interpretation, namely that bout.metric = 1 with closedbout = FALSE counts only the epochs within a bout that meet the criteria toward MVPA (periods of inactivity, for instance, would be excluded).

I think your explanation in this email is helpful, and could be included in the manual, something like.:

"The code for metric 2 only evaluates whether the bout criteria is met for an entire window and then counts all epochs within that window towards the bout, including the inactivity breaks.
Metric 1 in combination with closedbout=FALSE, is different in that it only counts the epochs that meet the criteria towards MVPA. Hence why it is called closedbout=FALSE (the gaps in the bout are not closed). This is why metric 2 provides longer bouts compared with metric 1 + closedbout=FALSE. Note that closebout = TRUE only affects metric 1, the other metrics are unaffected."
